_about: General guidance for the pet care companion (F20): typical healthy weight ranges and a general vaccination and deworming outline. Approximate values from common breed standards and general veterinary guidance, for orientation only; each vet's schedule comes first. Never medicine names or doses.

dog.what: Third core puppy vaccine and rabies vaccine
Yearly boosters, as your vet advises

cat.what: Second core kitten vaccine and rabies vaccine
Yearly boosters, as your vet advises

bird.what: No routine vaccines for pet budgies, lovebirds, cockatiels, finches or canaries in India. Book a first check with an avian vet in the first month, then yearly.

deworming.dog: Puppies are usually dewormed every 2 weeks until 3 months old, then monthly until 6 months, then as your vet advises. Ask your vet which product and amount.
deworming.cat: Kittens are usually dewormed every 2 weeks until 3 months old, then monthly until 6 months, then as your vet advises. Ask your vet which product and amount.
deworming.bird: Only if an avian vet finds worms, for example after a droppings test. Never deworm a bird without a vet.

bird: Sitting fluffed up at the bottom of the cage
Breathing with the tail bobbing, or clicking sounds
Not eating or drinking for a day
Bleeding or a broken blood feather
Watery droppings for more than a day
dog: Repeated vomiting or blood in vomit or stool
Swollen, hard belly or trying to vomit with nothing coming up
Not drinking, or no urine for a day
cat: Straining in the litter box without passing urine
